overall.note: Six of eight units can go to engineering now (1 Ship, 5 Ship with fixes). Step-up (ST-1) and the deletion lifecycle (DL-1) each have one Major that needs a small design or product decision first.

severityDefinitions.Blocker: Prevents a core task, exposes data or security, fails WCAG 2.2 AA in a way that blocks people, or cannot be built without the designer.
severityDefinitions.Major: A dead end, missing recovery, misleading state, or handoff contradiction likely to be built wrong; needs a design or product decision before build.
severityDefinitions.Minor: Polish, copy, consistency or spec hygiene a developer can fix during implementation without new design work.

issues.summary: No skip link: 8 sidebar tab stops precede page content on every desktop page. Add a 'Skip to content' link, visible on focus, targeting the h1.
issues.evidence: Rig keyboard order, Main 1280x800 (stops 1-8 sidebar, 9 = Change photo) in .design/qa-out/eval-results/auto/report.md; spec §3.2/§4.1 silent

issues.summary: Sidebar email truncation draws a half glyph before the generated ellipsis ('featherstonehau[g]…@'). Build it with EmailText (text-overflow), not the canvas pseudo-element.
In the clean state, the reserved action row and alert slot leave about 150-170 px of blank space under the name hint at every width; it reads as missing content and pushes the preview down on phones.
issues.evidence: shots-eval/Main@1440x900@dark@full.png (hint ends y≈530, Email h2 y=705), Main@390x844@full.png, Main@320x640@full.png; spec §1.5 rule 8, §4.2

issues.summary: On phones the live preview is about 550 px below the First name field, so it is off-screen while typing with a keyboard open, contrary to spec §1.4.
issues.evidence: shots-eval/Main@390x844@full.png (field y≈360-404, preview name label y≈947); spec §1.4 line 258

issues.summary: At 844x390 the crop area hits its 160 px floor and the Zoom slider scrolls out of view, though the spec sizes the crop so the slider stays in view.
Change-email step 1 shows about 100 px of empty dialog body because of the one-height rule; use it for useful copy.
aria-haspopup='dialog' sits on Change photo and Upload photo, which open the OS file picker, not a dialog.
The first-name error isn't reserved and moves the form 28 px, contrary to the stated 'states never move' rule; document field errors as the exception.
issues.evidence: #email-title 692→720 at 1440 and 1176→1204 at 390 (Main vs Profile-name-error), scripts/measure.mjs

issues.summary: Loading skeletons draw fewer lines than the loaded text at narrow widths, so content jumps 128-256 px at 320 (44 px at 1440) when data arrives, contrary to §4.3.
Empty reserved status slots make section gaps uneven (about 100 px at 1440 and 130 px at 320 after a section foot, against about 55 px elsewhere).

The spec runs step-up 'inside the same dialog' as the remove-passkey confirm, but the confirm is AlertDialog/AlertSheet and step-up is Dialog/Drawer. The transition, focus handoff and where a failure alert sits in the sheet are undefined.
issues.evidence: Spec §4.3 line 790, §8 rows 18-19; Security-remove-passkey and Stepup are drawn separately

issues.summary: The add-passkey failure 'No passkey added. The prompt was canceled or timed out.' gives no next step, against the area's own rule that errors say what to do.
The unknown-device advice omits checking passkeys and securing the mailbox; changing email needs a code from that mailbox.

Dead end when the code can't be received. Screen B offers only 'Use a passkey instead' (if available) and Cancel. Someone changing email off a lost work mailbox, past the 10-minute window and with no passkey, has no way forward and no explanation. Add 'Can't get the code?' with recovery options, and define a lost-mailbox recovery policy.
issues.evidence: Stepup-code.dc.html:42; shots-eval/Stepup-mobile@320x640.png; spec §4.4 Screen B, §4.2 change email flow

issues.summary: Screen A reserves screen B's height, leaving about 80-150 px of empty space under the note.
The locked state draws a focus ring around a static error paragraph, which reads as a button; §7.4 shows no ring for programmatically focused headings.
No rule for drawers with inputs when the on-screen keyboard is open (code, new email, rename, typed phrase); at 320x640 the delete drawer already fills the screen.
Empty reserved status slots leave about 85-125 px between sections, and the unsubscribe note floats 50-90 px below its group.
A language change reloads the interface, but nothing says where focus and scroll land afterwards or how the 'Saved. Richie is now in…' status survives the reload.
Only 'Emails from Richie' uses a fieldset with the h2 inside the legend; the other sections don't. Use one pattern.
App identity is a letter tile only; no rule for using the client's registered logo (LogoUri) or showing its website or publisher. Optional.
The delete dialog footer is right-aligned with unequal buttons, but the spec requires .is-even equal halves; .is-even exists in no board and no CSS rule.
The download description says 'sessions', against the spec's one-name rule ('device', not 'session').
The deletion consequences never say you can't use Richie with this account any more; a generic account-level line keeps to the PO rule. Flag workspace ownership on deletion to product.
Localisation and matching tolerance of the typed phrase 'delete my account' are unspecified.
issues.evidence: Spec §4.7 Field row; Language offers de, es, fr, pt-BR, ka (§4.5)

issues.summary: At 200% zoom and at 844x390 the fixed header and footer leave about 130-150 px of body; the typed field, which has initial focus, starts out of view.

Export token lifecycle undefined and can dead-end. A 'used' /export token goes to /export/expired, yet the expired-download page and the ready email send people back to /export for a new download. Nothing leads back for someone who lost the day-30 email, and identity sign-in for an address deleted in the last 30 days is unspecified.
Deletion-pending doesn't show which account is scheduled (no account chip, unlike Export-request).
'Keep my account' always goes to the Richie app root, dropping the sign-in's return URL (a deep link or an OAuth authorize request).
Several states are copy-only, and the expired-page titles differ between §3.1 and §4.8.
The cheerful, tongue-out shiba heads the 'Your account will be deleted' page; use a neutral pose or a badge.

crossCutting.summary: Two sources of truth: the §6.2 tables are admitted stale, §7.2 overrides the built CSS (and DP-1 shows real drift), and 81 spec lines carry internal QA IDs. Sync and clean before handoff.
crossCutting.evidence: Spec lines 1174, 1414; grep of A-/B-/C-/R- references

crossCutting.summary: §8 row 18 'Set dismissible so an outside click doesn't close it' reads backwards; suiss dismissible enables backdrop dismissal. Write dismissible={false}.
crossCutting.evidence: Spec line 1570; suiss-blocks-catalog.md §2.8 (confirm: dismissible defaults to false)

strengths: The live 'How customers see you' messenger: a product-specific signature that explains why your name and photo matter. It is workspace-neutral and aria-hidden with a sr-only summary, and it holds in dark, in forced colours and at 320 px.

Measured state discipline: reserved slots keep the following headings fixed across saved, failed, removed, waiting and failed-passkey states; dialogs keep one height; there is no horizontal overflow from 320 px to 200% zoom; axe found nothing critical or serious in either theme.

Security-grade flows and copy mapped to suiss: step-up with real numbers and the countdown in the button, readonly plus aria-disabled instead of disabled, confirmations that say what stops working, inline Undo instead of timed toasts, computed contrast, and a recipe-to-component handoff table whose components exist in the guide.
mustFix: ST-1: add a 'Can't get the code?' path to step-up screen B and define lost-mailbox recovery, so changing an email you can no longer read is not a dead end.

DL-1: define /export token reuse and expiry so 'Request a new download' can't land on the expired page, and add a route back to the export for people who lost the day-30 email (from identity sign-in or sign-up for a recently deleted address).
